text.p: TORONTO, July 31 Reuter) - The following are top headlines from selected Canadian newspapers. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
THE GLOBE AND MAIL: Justice takes a hammering: Judge decries sytematic abuse of rights in case that sent two men to jail in contract kiling
-Judge tough on native protesters: Gustafsen standoff hurt democracy
-Suicide bombers hit Jewish market: Carnage of deadly double blasts knocks Middle East peace process off course
-Shun distinct society, business group urges: Paper proposes premiers take unity lead
-Prostate cancer victims given new lease on life: Radiation plus hormone therapy boosts survival rates
-Laidlaw to buy Texas firm: Offers $312-million (U.S.) for provider of doctors' services to hospital emergency rooms
-Reichmann team makes first major property deal: Camdev to buy 3 Toronto office buildings for $81-million
-Sanctions ambush firms in Burma: Canadians thought they could do business anywhere. But Ottawa has turned the tables by targeting one of Asia's most noted dictatorshiips.
-CAI posts rare 2nd-quarter profit: Lower operating expensesoffset decline in revenue
-Laidlaw to expand health business in US$400M deal: All-cash offer wins backing of Dallas-based EmCare holdings
-Philip Reichmann puts O&Y back on real estate map
